name: Velarok
summary: Velarok Windblade is a lone human swordsman camped amid the ash and cinder of Searing Gorge, flanked by the mutilated corpses of Dark Iron dwarves. He seeks vengeance against the local Dark Irons for the brutal murder of his father, recruiting passing travelers to forge a weapon of retribution. His single-minded hunger for vengeance drives everything he asks of those who help him.

sections.title: A Son's Vengeance
sections.body: Found southeast of Thorium Point, Velarok Windblade presents himself as a grieving human warrior stranded in the perilous wastes of the Searing Gorge. Surrounding his camp are the bloody, battered corpses of Dark Iron dwarves who crossed his blade. According to Velarok, these clan dwarves slaughtered his father in cold blood. Consumed by hatred, he enlists travelers to gather materials to assemble the Torch of Retribution, an enchanted weapon of vengeance against the Dark Irons and the minions of Ragnaros.

sections.title: The Deceiver Unmasked
sections.body: The tale of a slain father is entirely a fabrication. Once the Torch of Retribution is fully assembled and energized, the human illusion shatters, exposing the figure as Velarok the Deceiver—a cunning drake of the black dragonflight. Having manipulated mortals into undermining the Dark Iron dwarves for the brood's own designs, Velarok spares his useful pawns out of amusement, leaving behind petty trinkets through his servant before taking wing toward Blackrock Mountain.

faq.answer: Velarok Windblade initially appears to be a vengeful human swordsman camping southeast of Thorium Point in Searing Gorge, seeking retribution against the Dark Iron clan for his father's demise.

faq.q: Why is Velarok surrounded by dead dwarves?
faq.answer: The mutilated Dark Iron remains scattered around his camp are the grim evidence of the blood feud he says he is waging against the clan for his father's death.

faq.q: What is the Torch of Retribution?
aliases: what is the torch of retribution
faq.answer: It is an enchanted torch assembled from rare materials gathered across Searing Gorge in the name of vengeance. Velarok has his helpers collect the pieces, combines and enchants them himself, and then binds the finished torch to the one who helped him.

faq.q: Why does Velarok disguise himself as a human?
faq.answer: Disguising as a human allows him to recruit Alliance and Horde adventurers without drawing suspicion. Black dragons frequently use mortal guises to orchestrate proxy strikes against their enemies, such as the Dark Iron servants of Ragnaros.

faq.q: Where does Velarok go after revealing himself?
faq.answer: Upon revealing his true dragon form as Velarok the Deceiver, he takes flight and heads toward Blackrock Mountain to rejoin his brood, leaving his mortal servant to award the adventurers who assisted him.

faq.q: Does Velarok attack when his disguise drops?
faq.answer: No. Velarok considers the adventurers' unwitting service amusing and satisfactory. Rather than destroying them, he spares their lives and permits them to receive minor trinkets from his servant.

angles.text: Velarok's tale of a murdered father and a son's vengeance plays on the ideals of filial duty and righteous retribution that many humans hold dear.

Dark Iron dwarves are enemies of Ironforge, and a stranger's vow of vengeance against them may find ready sympathy among Bronzebeards, though the Searing Gorge breeds more cunning evils than the Dark Irons alone.
